reading.title: Plate Tectonics and Mountain Formation
reading.passage: The theory of plate tectonics has fundamentally transformed our understanding of Earth's dynamic geology. The Earth's lithosphere is divided into several rigid plates that constantly move at rates of a few centimeters per year, driven by convection currents in the underlying mantle. When two continental plates collide, the immense compressional forces create dramatic geological features, most notably mountain ranges. The Himalayas, which continue to rise at approximately 5 millimeters annually, exemplify this process. As the Indian and Eurasian plates converge, crustal material is compressed and uplifted, forming the world's highest mountain chain. This collision began roughly 40 million years ago and continues today, demonstrating that mountain-building is an ongoing geological process. Additionally, plate boundaries generate significant seismic activity, as the accumulated stress is periodically released through earthquakes. Understanding these mechanisms has enabled scientists to predict volcanic eruptions and assess earthquake hazards in tectonically active regions, providing crucial information for urban planning and disaster mitigation in vulnerable areas.

유체가 가열되어 상승하고 냉각되어 하강하는 순환 운동

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the primary force that drives the movement of tectonic plates?
questions.explanation: passage의 두 번째 문장에서 'driven by convection currents in the underlying mantle'라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the Himalayas?
options: They were formed by volcanic activity
They stopped growing millions of years ago
They are still in the process of being formed
They are located where oceanic plates collide
questions.explanation: passage에서 '5 millimeters annually' 상승하고 있으며 'continues today'라고 했으므로, 히말라야는 현재도 계속 형성되고 있음을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.q: The word 'exemplify' in the passage is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: 'exemplify'는 '전형적인 예를 보여주다' 또는 '...의 좋은 예가 되다'라는 뜻으로, 히말라야가 산맥 형성 과정의 전형적인 사례임을 나타냅니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention the rate at which the Himalayas continue to rise?
options: To explain why mountain building is no longer occurring
To demonstrate that plate tectonics is an active and ongoing process
To argue that the Indian plate is moving faster than other plates
To show that seismic activity is decreasing over time
questions.explanation: 저자는 구체적인 상승률(5mm/year)과 '계속된다(continues today)'는 표현을 통해 산맥 형성이 과거가 아닌 현재진행형의 지질학적 과정임을 강조하고 있습니다.

sentences.original: The Earth's lithosphere is divided into several rigid plates that constantly move at rates of a few centimeters per year, driven by convection currents in the underlying mantle.
sentences.paraphrase: Convection currents occurring in the mantle propel the rigid plates composing Earth's lithosphere to move continuously, with displacement occurring at a rate of several centimeters annually.
sentences.tip: 능동태→수동태 전환, 'driven by'를 주절의 동사로 변환, 시간 표현 구조 변경

sentences.original: When two continental plates collide, the immense compressional forces create dramatic geological features, most notably mountain ranges.
sentences.paraphrase: The collision of continental plates results in the generation of powerful compressional forces, which in turn produce dramatic geological formations such as mountain ranges.
sentences.tip: 원인-결과 구조를 명사화, 'collide'→'collision', 'create'→'result in the generation of'로 동의어 치환

sentences.original: This collision began roughly 40 million years ago and continues today, demonstrating that mountain-building is an ongoing geological process.
sentences.paraphrase: The persistence of this collision from approximately 40 million years in the past to the present day serves as evidence that mountain formation constitutes a continuous geological phenomenon.
sentences.tip: 시간 표현 복잡화, 'continues'→'persistence', 'demonstrates'→'serves as evidence', 'ongoing process'→'continuous phenomenon'

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer spending more time with friends. Others prefer spending more time with family. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: I personally prefer spending time with my family over friends because family relationships provide a deeper sense of belonging and support.
Family members know me throughout different stages of my life, so they understand my values and can offer more meaningful advice when I face challenges.
For example, when I was stressed about my college application, my parents not only listened to my concerns but also helped me prepare by reviewing my essays multiple times.
Friends are important too, but they tend to change more frequently, whereas family bonds are typically lifelong and unconditional.
That's why I believe investing time in family relationships is ultimately more valuable for long-term happiness and stability.

listening.title: Economics Lecture: Supply and Demand
listening.script: Professor: Today we're going to explore one of the most fundamental concepts in economics—supply and demand. So, let's start with the basic principle. Demand refers to the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing to purchase at a given price. Supply, on the other hand, is the quantity that producers are willing to offer at that price. Now, here's the interesting part: these two forces interact to determine market equilibrium. When demand exceeds supply, prices tend to increase, right? Producers see an opportunity to profit, so they increase production. Conversely, when supply exceeds demand, prices fall, and producers are incentivized to reduce output. Let me give you a practical example. During the COVID-19 pandemic, there was a sudden surge in demand for personal protective equipment, especially masks and hand sanitizer. However, production capacity couldn't keep up immediately, so we experienced severe shortages. Prices skyrocketed. Eventually, as manufacturers ramped up production, the supply increased, and prices stabilized. This is supply and demand in action. So remember, this equilibrium isn't static—it's constantly shifting based on consumer preferences and production capabilities.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the lecture?
options: How supply and demand determine market prices
The causes of the COVID-19 pandemic
questions.explanation: 교수가 처음부터 'supply and demand'라는 기본 개념을 설명하겠다고 명시했으며, 전체 강의가 이를 중심으로 진행됩니다.

questions.q: According to the professor, what happens when demand exceeds supply?
questions.explanation: 교수가 명확하게 'When demand exceeds supply, prices tend to increase'라고 설명했습니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor mention the pandemic and PPE shortages?
options: To explain the history of mask production
To provide a real-world example of supply and demand dynamics
To discuss health and safety protocols
questions.explanation: 교수가 '실제 사례를 드리겠습니다(Let me give you a practical example)'라고 명시하고 팬데믹 상황을 수요초과→공급부족→가격상승→공급증가→가격안정화의 완벽한 공급-수요 사이클을 설명하는 예시로 사용했습니다.
